;Armed conflicts and attacks
*[[Syrian Civil War]]
**The son of [[Islamic State of Iraq and the Levant|ISIL]] leader [[Abu Bakr al-Baghdadi]] is killed in a [[suicide attack]] mission in [[Homs]], western [[Syria]], or in a Russian bombing of a cave. [https://www.voanews.com/amp/islamic-state-media-announces-death-leader-al-baghdadi-son/4465613.html (VOA News)]

;Disasters and accidents
*[[List of shipwrecks in 2018|Shipwrecks in 2018]], [[Disasters in Indonesia]]
**[[Sinking of MV Sinar Bangun|Sinking of MV ''Sinar Bangun'']]
***Authorities call off the search for 164 missing after the ferry sank in [[Lake Toba]]. Only three bodies have been recovered after the disaster. Although the wreck has been located, rescuers lack the equipment to raise it or attempt to retrieve any bodies inside. [http://newsinfo.inquirer.net/1006749/grief-and-prayers-as-search-for-sunken-indonesian-ferry-ends (''Inquirer'')]
**Ferry MV ''KM Lestari Maju'' sinks while ''en route'' to Pamatata in [[Selayar Islands|Selayar]], [[South Sulawesi]], [[Indonesia]], with 48 vehicles and 139 passengers on board. At least 12 fatalities are reported. [https://www.channelnewsasia.com/news/asia/indonesia-ship-sinks-4-dead-after-in-south-sulawesi-10495294 (Channel NewsAsia)]
*[[List of major power outages#2018|Major power outages]]
**[[Azerbaijan]]'s largest blackout since 1991 affects most of the country. [https://apnews.com/1864cb80fd4840eaa0855d2c8919d8be (AP)]
*A pedestrian bridge collapses onto railway lines in [[Mumbai]], injuring five. An approaching train is able to perform an emergency stop before colliding with the wreckage. Thousands of commuters are left stranded throughout the city. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-asia-india-44693602 (BBC)]

;Health and environment
*[[Seattle]] becomes the first major [[U.S.]] city to ban plastic straws and utensils in all bars and restaurants. [https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/british-columbia/seattle-bans-plastic-straws-and-utensils-in-restaurants-1.4732117 (CBC)]
*[[2018 Eastern Canada heat wave]]
**A heat wave throughout Eastern Canada kills six people in [[Montreal]]. [https://www.ctvnews.ca/canada/extreme-heat-blankets-5-provinces-linked-to-6-deaths-in-montreal-1.3997597 (CTV)]

;Law and crime
*[[Catholic sexual abuse cases in Australia]]
**[[Catholic Church|Roman Catholic]] [[Archbishop]] of [[Roman Catholic Archdiocese of Adelaide|Adelaide]], [[Philip Wilson (bishop)|Philip Wilson]], is sentenced to 12 months in detention for covering up child sexual abuse in the 1970s. [[Pope Francis]] appoints [[Port Pirie]] Bishop [[Gregory O'Kelly]] as [[Apostolic Administrator]], but with special near-full powers to govern the Archdiocese, though for now Wilson is still the Archbishop. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-australia-44692396 (BBC)]
*[[LGBT rights in the United Kingdom]]
**[[Theresa May]] announces a ban on [[conversion therapy|gay conversion therapy]]. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-44686374 (BBC)]
*[[Economy of the United Kingdom]]
**The [[UK]]'s [[Financial Reporting Council]] launches an investigation into financial services provider [[KPMG]] over its most recent audit of [[Convivality]], the defunct owner of retail chain [[Bargain Booze]]. [http://www.itv.com/news/2018-07-03/accounting-watchdog-probes-kpmg-over-conviviality-audit-following-collapse/ (ITV)]
*[[1Malaysia Development Berhad scandal]]
**Former [[Malaysia]]n [[Prime Minister of Malaysia|Prime Minister]] [[Najib Razak]] is arrested for allegedly misusing state funds. [https://www.cnn.com/2018/07/03/asia/razak-malaysia-arrest-intl/index.html (CNN)]
*A bomb kills three oil survey workers and injures five more near [[Dera Bugti]] in [[Baluchistan]], [[Pakistan]]. [https://newsok.com/article/feed/3590488/bomb-kills-3-oil-company-employees-in-southwestern-pakistan (AP via NewsOK)]
*[[Cheshire Police]] in [[England]] arrest a female healthcare professional on suspicion of murdering eight babies and attempting to murder six more at [[Countess of Chester Hospital]]. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-england-merseyside-44696813 (BBC)]

;Politics and elections
*[[Directive on Copyright in the Digital Single Market]]
**The [[Italian Wikipedia]] blocks all articles in protest of the [[European Union]]'s copyright law. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-europe-44696302 (BBC)] [https://www.thelocal.it/20180703/wikipedia-italy-blackout-eu-copyright-directive-reform (''The Local'')]
*[[Tunisian local elections, 2018]], [[Women in Tunisia]]
**Souad Abderrahim becomes the first woman to be elected as Mayor of [[Tunis]], the capital of [[Tunisia]]. [https://www.nytimes.com/aponline/2018/07/03/world/middleeast/ap-ml-tunisia-islamic-mayor.html (''The New York Times'')]

;Science and technology
*[[Discoveries of exoplanets]]
**The [[European Southern Observatory|European Southern Observatory's]] [[Very Large Telescope]] captures an image of [[PDS 70|PDS 70b]], making it the first clear image of a [[planet]] forming from the disk of gas and debris surrounding its host star. [https://www.nbcnews.com/mach/amp/ncna888521 (NBC News)]

;Sport
*[[2018 FIFA World Cup]]
**[[England national football team|England]] beats [[Colombia national football team|Colombia]] 4–3 in [[Penalty shoot-out (association football)|penalty shoot-out]] to advance to the [[2018 FIFA World Cup knockout stage#Quarter-finals|quarter-finals]] of the competition. It is the first time England has won a penalty shootout in a [[FIFA World Cup|World Cup]] match. [https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football/world-cup/england-vs-colombia-penalty-shootout-who-scored-kane-goal-video-watch-eric-dier-a8429861.html (''The Independent'')]
